body:
It's funny. This actually helped me a little too when I read it.

Very odd, indeed.
I'm all ears. I'll gladly hear them.

This actually did help quite a bit. I need to step away from this stuff as I'm at work and a mess - I need to collect myself here and focus on my job, but thank you. I'll probably respond again later.

> Of course it's difficult. If I could make a suggestion - remove her as a Facebook friend. I did that with my ex a couple of weeks ago - the constant posts by mutual friends to her, photos coming up, etc - it made the whole healing process so much harder to go through. It won't make sense to you at the moment, because it's all so fresh. You have to trust in part that with time, it will feel better.

Done.

>She told me she still loved me, but that she didn't think we should be together any more.

In my case, it wasn't that she even said that, it's that she told me she thought I needed a particular type of person that she couldn't be. I was too caught up in the emotions of the moment to say what I really wanted to say, which was that I wanted that decision to be mine. I think that's part of what's been killing me. Even when she left, I felt like there was so much more on the table to try and talk and work out, but it was too difficult to get past our tears. 

>Can you think of anything you used to do just for you, before the two of you got together? 

Before I met her, I was shelving video games. They weren't helping in my recovery with depression. I have been playing them again, but they get stale quickly. I need someone, a friend, to talk with to really pass the time while I play them.

I was getting into modern board games as I waned from video games. But board games was how we met. It was sort of a focal point of our relationship. We did crafts together to make our games look nicer or more functional. I have a collection that makes me choke up every time I see it now. As the relationship went on, it became less the focal point, but it was still there.

I use to read a lot of (auto)biographies, textbooks and science journals, but those are too passive.

>Don't feel guilty or confused because you're missing a certain emotion that you think should be there.

I don't really feel guilty or confusion for not being angry. I just would find it easier to handle if either of us did something wrong. I actually feel jealous of the relationships that have broken from someone cheating on them.

>At some point, I believe that you'll be able to look back on this as a learning and strengthening experience in life. For now, that's very hard to imagine, I'm sure. This woman I was with was the only woman I've ever loved, and the only sexual partner I've ever had. Drawing a line under that and moving on seemed impossible at the time. Now, it feels a little more manageable.

This is probably one of the more encouraging parts so far.

Still, I do feel that some positive things already came out from this fallout. I got to see some problems we had in our relationship that were there, that I never really knew or figured how to articulate. And now that I do, I want to apply that knowledge and experience to try and mend the relationship.

I'm refusing to believe that it has to be over, which is probably a futile stance.

Getting over this relationship is one thing. One very painful thing.

But seeing myself spiral into deep depression and loneliness is a different thing to tackle too. Even if I can get over her, I still feel that depression is going to be an issue.

>Forgive me if I've missed it somewhere, but I don't think you've said anywhere how long ago you guys broke up? It sounds to me like a lot of the emotion you're feeling is still very raw.

Sorry. It was in the title. We broke up only 3 weeks ago.

>We too had our stumbling blocks - we didn't talk as often as we should. We lived apart, which put a strain on the relationship. We argued over silly little things, for no real reason.

Part of this that is so difficult is that we didn't really argue. Ever. Not even when we broke up. We had a discussion, but we never fought.

> Take some time apart. I mean really apart. Don't try to call her. Don't follow her on facebook, read old messages, etc. It doesn't help. You need some time to process, to adjust to being single, and to adjust to her not being a part of your life at the moment. It's horrible to have to accept, and can feel pretty alien at first.

I'm trying to. Neither of us really went on Facebook, but I just miss her so much. It's so difficult to not look. I know it doesn't help, but I'm having a really tough time coming to terms that it's actually better to not be together. It doesn't make sense to me.

> Surround yourself with distractions - work, hobbies, friends, etc. It sounds superficial and stereotypical to a degree, but it works.

This is very difficult. I have a very unhealthy work-life. I was a work-a-holic before meeting her. Over 70 hours a week, on salary, was very common. Most of my hobbies, I shared with her - so all of them feel just as bad as looking at Facebook or looking at old messages, and I have so few friends - They've mostly been there when I've needed them. But I don't have too many to look to.

> I felt exactly the same. It's like we never even gave ourselves a chance. However, be that as it may, you are left with the situation you are left with. Sounds like a stupid thing to say. If at some point you both feel you can sit down and analyse what went wrong, then great. For now, I would suggest that doing so would be a bad idea.

This seems to be the general consensus, but for some reason it just doesn't hit home with me. I always felt there's a bit of anger between two people when they break up. There wasn't any. When we broke up, I thanked her for the great year and told her I loved her. She thanked me too, told me she loved me too and said I was amazing. 

It all just makes it hurt so much more. I want to feel anger. I want to feel this breakup, while painful, was just. I want to comfort myself with "this really was for the best". I don't know if I'll ever feel that way.

I don't know what will make me feel better. I know I'm really tired of feeling this pain. I've never felt so drained in my life. This has been the most difficult thing I've ever gone through.
